Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 31st January 2026
 
 
A Chara,   
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under 
Section 136 & 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s 
Monthly Management Report for January 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across 
various departments of Louth County Council.  
  
Here is a summary of key achievements and actions under various directorates from the Chief 
Executive Report for January 2026:  
.  
1. Financial Management and System Support  
• 
The financial management report outlines the expenditure and income of Louth County Council 
as of January 30, 2026.  
• 
Total actual expenditure to date: €13,966,544 against a budget of €203,652,265 (7% spent).  
• 
Total actual income: €46,576,018 against a budget of €203,652,265 (23% invoiced).  
• 
852 support calls logged in January 2026, with an 86.85% completion rate.  
• 
13% of inbound emails identified as potentially harmful due to phishing and spam.  
2. Economic Delivery  
• 
An open call is in place for businesses who wish to take part in the Age Friendly Business 
Program workshops.  
• 
Over 90 applications received for the Festival Grant Initiative, currently under assessment.  
• 
Collaboration with Meath and Kildare for the development of Brigid’s Way pilgrimage route.  
• 
The Association of Town and City Management (ATCM) confirmed that Drogheda has once 
again been awarded Purple Flag status  
• 
The Council has introduced a Rates Waiver Scheme for 2026  
• 
Planning and Development   
• 
90 planning applications received in December 2025, 81 deemed valid.  
• 
67 applications determined, with a refusal rate of 10.45%.  
• 
17 planning enforcement complaints investigated, with 16 cases resolved through negotiation.  
• 
€269,655 recouped from the Built Heritage Investment Scheme for various projects.  
• 
A Chief Executive’s Report has been prepared on submissions received during the public 
consultation period for the Pre-Draft Strategic Issues Paper for the new Louth County 
Development Plan 2027 - 2033.  
3. Operations and Environmental Delivery  
• 
Major drainage remediation efforts included cleaning gullies and addressing flooding issues 
during and after Storm Chandra.  
• 
Routine maintenance activities include litter picking, road repairs, and public space upkeep on 
going.  
• 
Significant pothole repairs conducted across various locations in Dundalk and Drogheda.  
• 
Illegal dumping addressed with the removal of multiple loads of waste from various sites.  
• 
Waste Enforcement Activities, 21 complaints received and investigated, all related to waste.  
• 
Water Pollution, 12 complaints received, with investigations ongoing.  
• 
Air and Noise Pollution, 6 complaints and 3 noise pollution cases reported.  
• 
Discharge Licences, 13 inspections carried out for Section 4 Discharge Licences.  
• 
Control of Dogs, 35 dogs processed through the pound, with 3 rehomed.  
• 
Dog Licences, 530 licences sold, with 115 notices issued for licence production.  
• 
Community Climate Action Fund: 51 applications received for funding, totalling €2,360,344.37.  
• 
There where 387 incidents for quarter 2 in 2025 by the fire service.  
4. HR, Corporate & Community Delivery   
• 
In January 2026 the Customer Services team dealt with 19,285 queries inclusive of 9,780 calls, 
1,185 e-mails and 8,320 counter queries. 11,346 (59%) of queries received were dealt with at 
first point of contact  
• 
Age-Friendly Housing: Site visit to Connolly’s Field for a new housing development for those over 
55, 70 homes to be made available.

6. Major Capital Projects and Infrastructure Delivery  
• 
Urban regeneration projects: Ongoing projects include the St. Nicholas Quarter 
and Longwalk Urban Framework Plan.  
• 
Active Travel projects: €4 million allocated for active travel and safe routes to schools projects.  
• 
Flood Defence and Coastal Erosion Projects  
• 
Dundalk Flood Relief Projects: Ongoing assessments and public participation planned for Q1/Q2 
2026.  
• 
Carlingford and Greenore Flood Relief: Developing project briefs based on recent flood events 
and survey data.  
  
I would like to conclude by expressing my sincere appreciation for the exceptional commitment, 
resilience, and professionalism demonstrated by the entire Louth County Council team. Across all 
directorates, staff continued to deliver high quality public services, maintain critical operations, and 
support our communities with dedication and pride. This was particularly evident during and after 
Storm Chandra, when teams undertook major works, cleared gullies, responded to flooding 
incidents, ensured public spaces, essential infrastructure were kept safe and functional.   
  
I encourage all members to read the full report, which reflects the breadth and impact of the 
remarkable work carried out across the organisation.

ArcGIS Online – Public Planning Register Map Viewer 
 
The LCC GIS Team recently updated the online Planning Register Map Viewers. These can be accessed from 
the Online Planning Application and Maps section user Services> Planning on the Louth County Council 
website.  
 
 
 
The data in the application is updated regularly to include all planning applications. There were 4901 views of 
the application between 01/01/2026 and 30/01/2026, an average of 169 views a day in January. 
 
 
Cyber Security Training  
 
January’s cyber security training demonstrated the impact a cyber security incident can have on a business. The 
video highlighted how a single successful spear-phishing attack can completely disable a business’s systems, 
leading to operational shutdown, financial loss and serious reputational damage. It reinforces the importance of 
staff vigilance — especially being cautious with suspicious links or attachments — because one careless click 
can enable a cyber-criminal to infiltrate and take control of critical systems.

The Táin Trail retraces the journey taken by Queen

Drogheda Awarded Purple Flag for 2026 
On Wednesday, 28th January, the Association of 
Town and City Management (ATCM) confirmed that 
Drogheda has once again been awarded Purple 
Flag status — an achievement driven by community 
energy, 
strong 
partnership 
and 
a 
genuine 
commitment to culture.  Similar to Blue Flags for 
beaches, Purple Flag is an international award 
recognising town centres that offer an appealing and 
enjoyable experience after 5.00pm.  Drogheda was 
assessed on 25th October, when two ATCM 
assessors visited during the Lú Festival of Light, 
meeting a broad range of partners contributing to the 
town’s evening offer. 
 
The renewal highlighted Drogheda’s community 
spirit and its strong arts and culture presence, with 
cultural anchors including the Barbican, Highlanes 
Gallery, Droichead Arts Centre, and The Kiosk 
Project Art Space.  Initiatives such as the Lú Festival 
of Light, Night Moves late cafés and the Dominican 
Church opening for The Cottage Market were also 
praised, along with the town’s growing partnership 
with Safe Gigs Ireland. 
 
Drogheda has held Purple Flag continuously since 
2019, coordinated by a working group involving the 
Council, Drogheda & District Chamber, Love 
Drogheda, An Garda Síochána, Safe Gigs Ireland, 
and a range of local night operators. 
What this means for the year ahead? 
• 
A clear confidence marker for residents, 
visitors and communications — helping 
shape a more assured perception of 
Drogheda after dark. 
• 
A stronger platform for funding, investment 
and promotion, supported by independent 
validation. 
• 
A framework for improvement across Purple 
Flag’s themes: appeal, place, movement, 
wellbeing and policy.

SEAI Monitoring & Reporting 2030 
The Monitoring & Reporting (M&R) system is 
now open for 2025 submissions. All public 
bodies are required to report their annual 
energy use and related data to SEAI. 
 
Each public body must meet three headline 
targets for 2030: 
 
• 
Increase energy efficiency by 50% 
compared 
with 
its 
baseline 
performance. 
• 
Reduce fossil-fuel CO₂ emissions by 
51% relative to the 2016–2018 
baseline period. 
• 
Achieve an overall energy-related 
CO₂ target for 2030, measured in 
tonnes. This target is calculated as 
the sum of the fossil CO₂ target and 
electricity emissions at the GHG 
baseline, 
minus 
the 
projected 
national electricity-sector emissions 
reductions by 2030.

validate all LCC MRPNs and GPRNs by
